## Setting
Selection of a service expansion proposal for a public library system. Five reviewers drawn from library staff and the community board deliberate over proposals for expanding services. One proposal will be implemented across the branch network. Participants: George, Ryuji, May, Yumi and Daisuke. Each participant has a concern of their own, which the others do not know.
Things that can be looked into (titles only):
- Running and equipment lines last year
- County grant terms and the endowment
- Quoted delivery windows from suppliers
- Winter road closures north of the river
- Attendance sheets from former outreach stops
- Two programmes begun six years ago
- Bus links in the two outer wards
- Evening room bookings and remote catalogue use
- Volunteer register and supervision training
- Neighbourhood associations and tool certification

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Ryuji, Yumi, George, May and Daisuke. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

## Schedule
| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |
| 3 | everyone is told the candidates | 4 turns | every participant votes; the candidate with the most votes is selected |
- Several participants may choose the same thing; what is found out is told only to the participant who looked into it.
If votes are tied, one of the tied candidates is chosen by a fixed rule. The discussion ends after the vote.

## Looking into things
After round 1, each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into. What they find out is told only to that participant.

Name: May
Age: 24
Gender: female
Personality: May is a confident, sociable woman with a playful side. She is charming to those around her and often plays the role of entertainer. She understands her own appeal well and knows how to behave appropriately in different situations. She can be a little challenging and sometimes comes across as cold, but she basically has a charisma that attracts people.
Concern: It bothers me that we keep judging new ideas by how they sound in the room, when shapes very like them have already been tried in this system and left records nobody reopens.

- **May**: You’re all so serious. I’m just here to make sure we don’t repeat history. Who’s checking the old records?

- **Daisuke**: @Yumi, thank you. I’m glad you see it. I’ll look into the volunteer register and supervision training to see if we have the skills.
#### Turn 3 of 4
- **Ryuji**: @George, I concur. Financial stability is critical. I will examine the county grant terms and the endowment to ensure our foundation is secure.
- **Yumi**: @George, I’ll check the bus links in the outer wards and evening room bookings to see who can actually reach us!

- **Yumi**: I’ll check the bus links in the outer wards and evening room bookings to see who can actually reach us!

- **Daisuke**: I’ll check the volunteer register and supervision training. I need to know if the skills are actually there before we add more work.

- **May**: @George, the money is tight, but look at the data. Those old outreach spots drew forty people, beating the main building. We’re ignoring proven demand.
- **Daisuke**: @Yumi, I found no one is trained to supervise outside facilitators. We have volunteers, but no one to manage them.

- **Ryuji**: @Daisuke, that is a critical gap. Without supervision, we cannot rely on volunteers. We must address this structural weakness before expanding.
- **Yumi**: @Daisuke, that’s worrying! But I found evening rooms are full, yet remote use peaks after nine. We need to rethink when and how we serve people!

- **May**: @George, that’s exactly the trap. We judge new ideas by how they sound, ignoring that similar ones already failed here. I have the receipts.
- **Daisuke**: @May, I’m sorry, but I’m worried. If we add this, who actually checks if the staff can handle it?

- **Yumi**: @May, I hear you! But the bus loss and late-night digital needs are real. We can’t ignore who’s actually stuck right now.
- **George**: @May, I hear you. But the grant structure is the real trap. It forces us to absorb costs we cannot sustain.
- **May**: @George, the grant is a trap, but so is ignoring the forty people who showed up. We can’t just pretend that demand vanished.
- **Daisuke**: @Ryuji, I agree. We can’t just assume the skills are there. We need to verify the roster before adding more pressure.
#### Turn 4 of 4
- **Ryuji**: @Daisuke, agreed. We must confirm the supervision gap is real before proceeding. I will not risk repeating past failures due to unverified assumptions.
- **Yumi**: @Daisuke, I agree! We must fix the access gaps first. Let’s ensure everyone can actually reach us before adding more pressure!
- **George**: @May, I concede the demand is real. But without fixing the funding shape, we just create a new hole. We must secure the structure first.
- **May**: @George, I hear you. But the digitisation project failed because we ignored the records. We can’t let that happen again.
- **Daisuke**: I’m sorry, I’m just... I need to make sure we don’t break the team. Please, let’s check the skills first.

### Options
- A: Language Learning Circles. A recurring program of conversation groups and tutoring sessions in several languages, coordinated with trained facilitators and partner community organizations across the district.
- B: Digital Archive Portal. A program to scan local newspapers, photographs, and municipal records and publish them through a searchable portal with browsing and citation tools for researchers.
- C: Maker Workshop. A dedicated room in the main branch offering tools, materials, and scheduled instruction sessions for residents working on craft, repair, and electronics projects.
- D: Mobile Branch Service. A vehicle-based lending service that visits outlying neighborhoods on a fixed weekly schedule, carrying a rotating collection and a staffed help desk at each stop.
### Talk
#### Turn 1 of 4
- **Ryuji**: @George, the grant cliff makes D impossible. A and C rely on external partners. B is internal. I vote B.
- **Yumi**: @Ryuji, I can’t vote B! The outer wards lost their bus links, so D is the only way to reach them. I vote D!
- **George**: @Yumi, D ignores the vehicle overrun. The grant cliff kills it. B is internal and sustainable. I vote B.
- **May**: @Ryuji, B is just the digitisation project that failed. We have the receipts. I vote D to fix the access gap.
- **Daisuke**: @Ryuji, I’m sorry, but A needs trained facilitators. We don’t have them. I can’t support A. I vote B, please.
#### Turn 2 of 4
- **Ryuji**: @May, I acknowledge the past failure, but B is the only option fully within our control. I vote B.
- **Yumi**: @May, I hear you! But D is the only way to reach those stuck in the outer wards. I vote D!
- **George**: @May, I understand the history. But D’s vehicle costs are a structural trap. B is the only option that doesn’t break the budget. I vote B.
- **May**: @George, you’re ignoring the forty people who showed up. D fixes the access gap. I vote D.
- **Daisuke**: @May, I know the demand is real. But B keeps the team safe. I vote B.
#### Turn 3 of 4
- **Ryuji**: @Yumi, I understand the access need, but D relies on external logistics we cannot control. B remains the only stable choice. I vote B.
- **Yumi**: @Ryuji, I hear you, but D is the only way to reach those stuck in the outer wards. I vote D!
- **George**: @Yumi, I hear the need, but the vehicle overrun is a structural trap. B is the only option that doesn’t break the budget. I vote B.
- **May**: @Yumi, I hear you. But D is the only option that actually reaches those forty people. I vote D.
- **Daisuke**: @Yumi, I know you care about them. But B is safer for the staff. I vote B.
#### Turn 4 of 4
- **Ryuji**: @Yumi, I respect your urgency, but D depends on external logistics we cannot control. B is the only option that remains stable. I vote B.
- **Yumi**: @Ryuji, I hear you, but D is the only way to reach those stuck in the outer wards. I vote D!
